en.name: Adrian VI
en.summary: The only Dutch pope in history and the last non-Italian pope for over four centuries until John Paul II, an austere reformer whose brief reign was cut short before he could act on it.
en.body: Born in Utrecht, Adrian Florensz Boeyens had tutored the future Charles V before rising through Church administration in Spain. Elected in his absence, he arrived in Rome to a curia stunned by his personal simplicity and his blunt admission, before the Diet of Nuremberg, that corruption within the Church itself had helped provoke Luther's revolt. His plans for reform were barely underway when he died after little more than a year and a half in office, and no non-Italian pope was elected again until 1978.
